title: Impact of Analyst Coverage on Firm Investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables)  

Rationale  
• Analyst coverage (x) is likely endogenous to firm investment (y): unobserved fundamentals can drive both.  
• Exogenous shocks to coverage stemming from broker mergers (z) provide quasi-random variation.  

Key Assumptions  
1. Relevance – Broker mergers must materially change the number of analysts covering affected firms: Cov(z,x) ≠ 0 (testable via first-stage F-statistic).  
2. Exclusion – Broker mergers affect firm investment only through the induced change in analyst coverage, not through any other channel (not directly testable but argued on institutional grounds).  
3. Independence – Conditional on controls (firm size, industry, past performance), the instrument is as-good-as-random.

## 2. R Code  
```r
# ---- Libraries ----
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)      # fast reading
  library(AER)        # ivreg
  library(lmtest)     # coeftest
  library(sandwich)   # robust vcov
})

# ---- 0. Read data ----
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s71_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 y = col_double(),
                 x = col_double(),
                 z = col_integer(),
                 controls = col_double()
               ))

# ---- 1. Baseline OLS (naïve) ----
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 2. Two-Stage Least Squares ----
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 3. First-stage diagnostics ----
first_stage <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics
fst_f <- first_stage["Weak instruments", "statistic"]  # Kleibergen-Paap rk F

# ---- 4. Alternative specification (robustness) ----
# Add squared control to flexibly soak up scale effects
df$controls_sq <- df$controls^2
iv_alt <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls_sq |
                  z + controls + controls_sq, data = df)
iv_alt_robust <- coeftest(iv_alt, vcov = vcovHC(iv_alt, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 5. Print results ----
cat("====== Baseline OLS (robust SE) ======\n")
print(ols_robust["x", ])

cat("\n====== 2SLS IV (robust SE) ======\n")
print(iv_robust["x", ])

cat(sprintf("\nFirst-stage Kleibergen-Paap F-statistic: %.2f\n", fst_f))

cat("\n====== Robustness check: 2SLS with quadratic control (robust SE) ======\n")
print(iv_alt_robust["x", ])
```

The script:
• Loads the data.  
• Runs naïve OLS for comparison.  
• Implements 2SLS with robust (HC1) standard errors.  
• Reports the Kleibergen–Paap first-stage F-statistic for instrument strength.  
• Adds a quadratic control as a robustness check.  
All key numerical outputs are printed clearly.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Greater analyst coverage alleviates information asymmetry, lowers external financing costs, and encourages investment.  

Magnitude: A one-standard-deviation increase in analyst coverage should raise investment by roughly 0.15–0.30 standard deviations (coefficient ≈ 0.20).  

Diagnostics:  
• First-stage F > 10, confirming instrument strength.  
• IV estimate larger than OLS (OLS downward-biased toward zero because firms with expected low investment may seek coverage).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use broker mergers as an instrument for analyst coverage.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased analyst coverage significantly boosts firm investment.
